newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-GARCIAPARRA, VAUGHN POWER RED SOX PAST ORIOLES.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-GARCIAPARRA, VAUGHN POWER RED SOX PAST ORIOLES.

text.p: Nomar Garciaparra smacked a pair of home runs and Mo Vaughn belted a two-run homer to power the Boston Red Sox to a 9-5 victory over the Baltimore Orioles on Thursday.

Garciaparra hit a three-run homer in the fourth inning off Baltimore starter Scott Kamieniecki that gave the Red Sox a 6-2 lead. He capped the scoring with a solo shot in the eighth off reliever Shawn Boskie.
It was the first two-homer game and the second four RBI outing for the rookie outfielder.
"I'm not a home-run hitter," said Garciaparra. "I don't think about that, hitting home runs. If they come, they come."

Vaughn hit his 19th homer in the third inning to tie the game at 2-2 and Tim Naehring drove in three runs for Boston. Reggie Jefferson had three doubles and reached base in all four plate appearance for the Sox.
Aaron Sele (7-5) allowed three runs and six hits over seven innings to pick up the win. Reliever Kerry Lacy gave up Baltimore's final two runs on a two-run blast by B.J. Surhoff in the eighth.
"Yes, they are in first place, and yes, we are a ways back, but we're playing hard and I think this series showed it," said Sele.
Kamieniecki (4-3) was torched for eight runs and nine hits over four innings. He walked four and struck out two in his shortest outing of the year.
In Cleveland, Jose Mercedes pitched eight strong innings as the Milwaukee Brewers snapped a six-game losing streak with a 6-2 victory over the Indians.
Mercedes (3-2), a late replacement for Scott Karl, limited the Indians to just six hits, three of which came in the ninth when he gave up Cleveland's first run.

He faced the minimum 24 batters through eight innings with the help of three double plays and a baserunning error by Omar Vizquel. Scheduled starter Karl was scratched because of stiffness in his upper right back.
The Brewers piced up single runs in the fourth and sixth inning before taking a 4-0 lead in the eighth Dave Nilsson's two-run homer.
Jeff Cirillo added a two-run double in the ninth for a 6-0 lead before the Indians finally broke through in the bottom of the inning.
Four other American League teams were in action Thursday against National League clubs in the first regular-season interleague contests in baseball history.
